items.statement: Final: a two-step molecular explanation of the complete N-propargylation
items.expected: Finally, use a computationally supported connected explanation to link the roles of the substrate, base and alkylating reagent through to the correct N-propargyl product. The authors' deprotonation followed by substitution is a reference; equivalent routes supported by actual evidence are acceptable. Merely showing isolated TSs/products or proposing an untested reaction type is insufficient.

items.statement: Final: distinguish local substitution difficulty from overall exergonicity
items.expected: Using the connected pathway and comparable energies, explicitly establish that subsequent N–C substitution has a more pronounced local activation requirement than the preceding near-reactant deprotonation, while the net conversion is exergonic. Correctly distinguish relative profile heights, local barriers from the respective precursors and the reaction ΔG; the authors' 16.2 is only an energy difference under their reference definition. Do not describe a negative relative TS G as an experimentally strictly barrierless reaction, or infer a quantitative rate from 89%/24h.
